scope: All seven complete source snapshots and three original authority hashes/lengths verified; every current SDK production file matched its frozen snapshot.

Full new FSReqCallback constructor/derived-lifetime body and new FileHandleReadWrap body inspected. For the five changed existing files, exact complete original-to-proposal diffs were read, with relevant surrounding lifecycle/template/C admission code.

This review closes the new FSReqCallback template/constructor and immutable unassigned/typed storage admission delta; it does not requalify unchanged ReadStart/ReadStop algorithms or whole shared VM/IO owners.

findings.assessment: The public constructing branch first instantiates the actual template receiver, then invokes present NewFSReqCallback behavior. IsTrue is strict primitive-boolean-only, not truthiness. Calling without new converts its receiver before the exact native args.IsConstructCall CHECK; no no-handler fallback is admitted for this kind.

findings.assessment: newFSReqCallbackInstance directly instantiates fsreqcallback and bypasses Request.construct. The FileHandle read caller now supplies BindingData.template_owner to that operation. The cached blank template object is never the native-attached returned receiver.

The new kind is appended, preserving all four old enum ordinals. Registry IDs, template constructors and cached instance arrays all have five entries; native name mapping and class-registration list include FSReqCallback. Provider8 matches original FSREQCALLBACK. Existing filehandle internal-field special handling remains unchanged.

Real generic physical UV storage precedes AsyncWrap hooks; after attached AsyncWrap, actual ReqWrap queue initialization, MakeWeak and initial Reset occur before use_bigint and the strong BindingData member. No completion Promise or detached BaseObjectPtr is created by NewFSReqCallback. Original null continuation and unused inline64-byte buffer require no active allocation or cleanup in this constructor-only unit.

findings.area: ordinary hook rethrow and fatal separation
findings.assessment: Only an attached, completed init hook producing ordinary JavaScriptException may continue the original void AsyncReset constructor path. Failed attachment, incomplete init hook, other typed errors or a fatal boundary escape to construction cleanup. The caller retains its receiver local throughout that continuation.

Successful native retain is recorded in binding_data and retired before ReqWrapBase unlink, matching the reverse original member order with default FSReqBase destructor at node_file.cc215. pointerData allocation failure occurs before increment. Under the live controller call, requireEngine only checks owner thread/current engine; there is no new guest call between strong-count increment and recording this member. General Init/continuation ownership is explicitly not exposed yet.

Unattached failure releases the unsubmitted C storage and destroys the native allocation. Attached failure uses the actual derived retire/destroy pipeline; entry_initialized gates queue unlink and binding_data gates its independent native release. Completion captures the original failure before cleanup. C storage has its own service entitlement; callback events can retain it independently after native wrapper retirement.

Configuration rejects mismatched Environment or controller, verifies a live shared call and retains the existing native Controller once. The Bundle releases it after cached instances/constructors and before its retained registry. No second service/worker/Engine is created. The internal/fs assembler must still configure it before exposing the constructor/template.

PI_UV_FS_UNASSIGNED is0; READ/OPEN/CLOSE remain1/2/3. storage_kind is assigned exactly once during allocation. Generic admission permits all implemented operations; existing typed allocations permit only their original operation. All four submission routes set the attempted operation only after their existing input/state checks. Invalid input leaves operation/storage state unmodified.

Reset leaves storage_kind immutable and retains its prior complete/dequeued/cleaned gates. Actual last-operation kind may remain observable until the next valid submission, as native request metadata can after Reset; it is not used as the generic admission restriction. Existing event fields/reference ownership and prior release-only event rules are unchanged. Entry.cancel still suppresses unsubmitted native cancellation.

findings.area: same brand versus concrete derived type
findings.assessment: FSReqCallback.unwrap requires both the template brand and exact derived destroy function identity. A FileHandleReadWrap intentionally using that same source template cannot be reinterpreted as FSReqBase.
